title: Youth Endowment Fund Youth Voice Officer 2026: Apply for a £34,200 Youth Engagement Role in London
summary: The Youth Endowment Fund (YEF) is accepting applications for a Youth Voice Officer (Maternity Cover) position in London, United Kingdom. This 12-month fixed-term opportunity is designed for someone with experience working directly with young people who is passionate about ensuring that young people s experiences, perspectives and ideas meaningfully influence work aimed at preventing youth violence. The successful candidate will join the Youth Endowment Fund s Youth Understanding team and play an important role in supporting the organisation s Youth Advisory Board (YAB) . Responsibilities range from planning and delivering activities for young people to providing pastoral and safeguarding support, facilitating lived-experience involvement, and working with communications colleagues to amplify young people s voices. The position offers an annual salary of £34,200 , alongside professional development funding, generous annual leave, pension contributions, flexible working hours and other employee benefits. It is based in Central London , with employees expected to work from the office for at least two days each week. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. on 7 October 2026 . About the Youth Endowment Fund The Youth Endowment Fund works to prevent children and young people from becoming involved in violence. Its approach combines research, evaluation, funding and testing interventions to identify effective approaches to violence prevention and help put that evidence into practice. A central part of this work is understanding how and why young people become involved in violence . YEF combines rigorous evaluations and research studies with the stories and perspectives of young people themselves. The organisation also believes young people should be central to the messages it communicates externally. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer The Youth Voice Officer will contribute directly to this mission by helping young people use their experiences and voices to shape, support and amplify YEF s work through its Youth Advisory Board . Youth Voice Officer 2026: Position Overview The main details of the opportunity are: Position: Youth Voice Officer (Maternity Cover) Organisation: Youth Endowment Fund Reports to: Youth Understanding Manager Salary: £34,200 per annum Contract: 12-month fixed-term maternity cover Location: Central London, United Kingdom Working arrangement: Hybrid, with at least two days per week in the London office DBS requirement: Enhanced DBS with Children s Barred List Application deadline: 5:00 p.m., 7 October 2026 The role requires regular direct engagement with children and young people, both online and in person. For this reason, an Enhanced DBS check with Children s Barred List is required. YEF states that having a criminal record does not automatically prevent someone from working for the organisation; disclosed information will be considered fairly and in relation to the requirements of the position. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer What Does the Youth Voice Officer Do? The Youth Voice Officer will work closely with young people, colleagues and external partners to ensure youth perspectives are embedded throughout YEF s activities. The position has three major areas of responsibility. 1. Co-Lead the Youth Advisory Board One of the primary responsibilities is helping to lead an accessible, safe and effective Youth Advisory Board . The successful applicant will be expected to: Plan, lead and review engaging activities for young people, including meetings and events. Build and maintain trusting relationships with Youth Advisory Board members. Provide pastoral support and care to YAB members. Support young people s personal development planning. Apply appropriate safeguarding practices. Help recruit and induct new Youth Advisory Board members. Participate in interviews and manage elements of YAB recruitment. Monitor members attendance and engagement. Coordinate Youth Advisory Board participation in external events. Youth Advisory Board members are young people aged 16 to 25 . Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer Most YAB activities take place online, but applicants should be comfortable with some evening work, normally around one to two evenings per week . YEF states that these meetings will finish no later than 7:45 p.m., with later starts on the previous or following day to recognise the additional working time. There may also be occasional weekend and in-person activities. Time off in lieu is provided for weekend work. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer 2. Champion Young People s Lived Experience Across YEF Another major component of the role is ensuring that young people s lived experiences genuinely contribute to YEF s work. The Youth Voice Officer will work with colleagues to create meaningful opportunities for Youth Advisory Board members to contribute to the organisation s priorities. Responsibilities include: Leading working groups focused on lived experience. Supporting young people to contribute to YEF s emerging priorities. Creating safe and trauma-informed environments. Helping young people feel confident and supported when communicating their experiences and opinions. Ensuring young people s voices are heard. Communicating back to young people about how their involvement has influenced the organisation. Developing positive relationships with relevant external providers. Helping young people in settings such as secure environments contribute their perspectives. Preparing Youth Advisory Board members to participate in external events and conferences. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer This makes the position particularly relevant to candidates interested in youth participation, youth advocacy, safeguarding, violence prevention, lived-experience engagement and social impact . 3. Amplify Youth Voices Through Communications The Youth Voice Officer will also collaborate with the YEF Communications team to help ensure young people s perspectives reach wider audiences. The successful applicant will help: Plan and create effective communications outputs. Serve as a bridge between the Youth Advisory Board and YEF s external communications team. Amplify young people s voices through social media and other media opportunities. Support young people in communicating their opinions, experiences and stories through different formats. Explore creative ways for young people to communicate. Collaborate with external companies and creative professionals on projects involving Youth Advisory Board members. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer The position therefore combines elements of youth work, communications, project coordination, safeguarding, advocacy and stakeholder engagement . Who Is YEF Looking For? YEF is seeking someone who genuinely believes in young people s potential and has practical experience supporting them. Experience Working With Young People Applicants should have worked with young people and understand the positive contribution they can make to social change. Candidates should have experience and knowledge of safeguarding processes and should be able to work flexibly according to young people s needs, including adapting plans at short notice when necessary. Job-Advert-Youth-Voice-Officer Passion for Helping Young People Be Heard The successful applicant should have experience supporting young people to communicate their experiences and stories in safe and strength-based ways . title: Mundus MAPP 2027–2029: Fully Funded Erasmus Mundus Master’s in Public Policy for European and International Students
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027–2029 Mundus MAPP cohort , offering prospective students the opportunity to pursue a two-year Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy across leading European universities, with a limited number of prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarships available to outstanding applicants from both EU and non-EU countries. The programme is designed to provide scholarly education and practical training for future academic and policy leaders in the public, private and non-profit sectors , with a particular focus on understanding how political institutions, processes and public policies operate from the global political economy through national and local levels, including European engagements. Key Details Programme: Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy – Mundus MAPP Cohort: 2027–2029 Duration: 24 months Study format: Full-time, in-person Study locations: Austria, Spain, the Netherlands and the UK, depending on the selected mobility track Scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship Maximum EMJM scholarship: €33,600 over 24 months Monthly scholarship contribution: €1,400 Tuition fee: €13,000 per academic year / €26,000 for the full programme Scholarship application deadline: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET Scholarship: No separate scholarship application is required. What is the Mundus MAPP Programme? Mundus MAPP is an Erasmus Mundus Master’s Programme in Public Policy delivered by a consortium of four institutions. The programme combines a common core of policy studies with specialised mobility tracks. Approximately 60% of the curriculum is common to all students , while 40% is delivered through track-specific modules . The programme also includes study visits, internships and research work across the two years. Mundus MAPP is a full-time in-person programme that allows students to tailor their learning experience through the selection of a mobility track. Students are exposed to different European academic traditions and policy contexts through study visits and internships. The programme has a strong practical component, including internships, spring courses/study trips and case-study-based teaching . These activities are intended to help students observe real-world policymaking, interact with practitioners, apply theoretical knowledge to practical policy problems, conduct research and build professional networks. Four Mundus MAPP Study Tracks Applicants may apply to one of four mobility tracks: 1. CEU-IBEI Track – Global Public Policy This track focuses on the policy process at the international and global level, including international organisations and global policy regimes. Students study at Central European University (Private University) in Vienna, Austria, in Year 1 , before continuing at Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals (IBEI) in Spain in Year 2 . 2. CEU-York Track – European Public Policy This track focuses on policy analysis, policymaking and problem-solving in the European Union, its member states and neighbourhood countries . Students study at Central European University in Vienna in Year 1 and continue at the University of York in the UK in Year 2 . 3. ISS-IBEI Track – Political Economy and Development This mobility track combines study at the International Institute of Social Studies (ISS) in the Netherlands and IBEI in Barcelona, Spain , with a focus on political economy and development. 4. ISS-York Track – Governance and Development This track combines study at ISS in the Netherlands and the University of York in the UK , focusing on governance and development. The four tracks offer different substantive focuses while maintaining a common core of policy studies. Important: Applicants may apply for only one mobility track . Erasmus Mundus Scholarship – What Does It Cover? The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship will be offered to outstanding applicants from both within and outside the EU. A limited number of EMJM scholarships are awarded to the highest-ranked applicants for the duration of the programme. The scholarship is calculated at €1,400 per month , corresponding to a maximum scholarship amount of €33,600 over 24 months . The monthly contribution is intended to assist students with travel, visa, installation, subsistence and other costs . EMJM scholarship recipients also receive a full tuition-fee waiver . Additional financial support may be available for students with individual needs depending on the level of disability/support required. Institutional Scholarships In addition to the EMJM scholarships, the Mundus MAPP Consortium will offer one Institutional Scholarship per study track . Recipients receive a 50% tuition fee waiver at the Year 1 and Year 2 institutions . The Institutional Scholarship does not include a stipend . Costs Not Covered by the EMJM Scholarship Applicants should budget carefully because the EMJM scholarship does not cover: Study Visit: approximately €600–€1,000 Winter School: approximately €600–€1,000 Travel and visa costs between the student s home country and consortium countries Travel costs when moving to the Year 2 university. The programme also strongly encourages applicants to seek external funding because only a small number of applicants will receive scholarships. Mundus MAPP Financial Aid and Scholarships Official Mundus MAPP website Who Can Apply? Mundus MAPP is open to European and third-country national students . Applicants must meet the programme s minimum admission requirements. Academic Requirements Applicants must have: A Bachelor s degree comprising at least three years of study from a recognised university or higher education institution. At least Class 2.1/Upper Second , where applicable. A minimum GPA of 3.17/4.0 or equivalent . Applicants are required to provide their GPA on a 4.0 scale. Candidates with degrees in the social sciences or equivalent are normally given preference. Applicants with a Bachelor s degree in Natural Sciences or Engineering are not eligible to apply . Applicants who already hold a Master s degree must also meet the required academic standard at Master s level. The programme notes that priority for scholarships is given to students who have not yet had the opportunity to study in a Master s degree programme . Mobility Requirement Physical mobility is compulsory for all enrolled students. Students must complete two study periods in two different countries , with each study period comprising a minimum of 30 ECTS . Both countries must be different from the student s country of residence at the application/enrolment stage. Compulsory mobility periods cannot be replaced by virtual mobility . Applicants will also need to provide proof of residence before enrolment. This is particularly important when selecting your mobility track. English Language Requirements Mundus MAPP does not require an English language certificate from citizens of several countries, including Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, South Africa, Tanzania, The Gambia, Liberia, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia and others , provided they have completed a Bachelor s or Master s degree taught exclusively in English. For other applicants, accepted tests include: TOEFL iBT: 95 or above IELTS Academic: 7 or above Cambridge C2 Proficiency: C2 or above Cambridge C1 Advanced: C1 or above Pearson PTE Academic: 76 or above Duolingo English Test: 130 or above. Important update for ISS applicants Applicants considering the ISS-IBEI or ISS-York tracks should pay particular attention to the Dutch visa requirements. For the 2027–2029 cohort, some applicants admitted to an ISS track may need to provide additional proof of English proficiency for their Dutch visa. The programme states that these are visa requirements, not admissions requirements . Applicants from Ghana and several other previously exempt countries may apply without a test result, but admission to the ISS tracks may be conditional until an accepted English test is submitted. The test must be provided no later than six weeks after receiving the official offer . Work Experience Is Not Required Work experience is not an eligibility requirement , although candidates with relevant work experience may be considered favourably. This means the programme can be relevant to both recent graduates and applicants who have already developed professional experience in public policy, development, government, international organisations, civil society, research or related areas. What Documents Do You Need? Applicants should prepare the following: 1. Online Application Form There are four application forms corresponding to the four mobility tracks. Applicants may apply for only one track. 2. Two Recommendation Letters Applicants must provide two official letters of recommendation , preferably with at least one from an academic. Referees receive an email after the application is submitted and have seven days to upload their recommendations. Applicants are advised to monitor the Applicant Portal and remind referees of the deadline. References sent by email, fax or regular post are not accepted. 3. Academic Records Applicants must upload electronic versions of their higher education academic records, including: Official English translation of the Bachelor s degree transcript Official English translation of the Bachelor s degree diploma/degree certificate Relevant Master s degree documents, where applicable. 4. Curriculum Vitae/Resume The CV should include a list of publications , if applicable. 5. Statement of Purpose The statement of purpose must be no more than 500 words and should highlight: Your reasons for applying to Mundus MAPP Your research interests Relevant academic and work experience Future career plans The study track to which you are applying. The programme specifically notes that, because of the high number of applications, longer statements will not be considered . 6. Proof of English Proficiency Where required, applicants must submit the relevant English language test as part of the online application. Late submission of test scores is not permitted. What Should You Know About the Application Process? Admissions to Mundus MAPP are centrally administered by Central European University Private University . Applications must be submitted to CEU PU through the specified online application process. It is not possible to apply to Mundus MAPP through another consortium university. Candidates complete the online application and upload the required supporting documentation. If you want to be considered for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship, you simply indicate your interest in the online application form . There is no separate scholarship application. How to Apply – Mundus MAPP 2027–2029 Mundus MAPP Application Deadlines Applicants should carefully select the deadline that applies to their circumstances. December 1, 2026 – 23:59 CET This is the key deadline for applicants who: Wish to be considered for financial aid/scholarships , or Are applying early as self-funded students. The first-round decisions, including EMJM scholarship decisions , will be available in the Applicant Portal on April 14, 2027 . April 15, 2027 – 23:59 CET Deadline for non-EU/EEA residents who do not wish to be considered for financial aid . July 1, 2027 – 23:59 CET Deadline for EU/EEA residents who do not wish to be considered for financial aid . For scholarship applicants, the important date to remember is December 1, 2026. View the official Mundus MAPP Admissions Calendar How Are Scholarships Awarded? The scholarships are awarded based on academic merit . Applicants who submit their application by the December 1, 2026 scholarship deadline will be asked in the online portal to indicate their interest in a potential scholarship. Because the number of scholarships is limited, applicants are strongly encouraged to explore additional funding opportunities. Important Advice for Prospective Applicants Start preparing early Do not wait until the deadline to begin collecting documents. Recommendation letters, official translations, academic records and English-language tests can take time. Choose your mobility track carefully Your application is for one specific mobility track , so applicants should review the curriculum, countries, institutions and specialisation associated with each track before submitting their application. Pay attention to the 500-word limit Your statement of purpose should be no more than 500 words . Use the limited space to clearly explain your motivation, academic and professional background, research interests, career plans and preferred track. Contact your referees early Recommendation letters must be uploaded within seven days after the application is submitted . Ask your referees in advance and make sure they know to check their spam folders for the automated email. Read the ISS visa requirements carefully If you are considering an ISS-IBEI or ISS-York track, check the additional Dutch visa-related English requirements before submitting your application. What Can Students Expect From the Programme? Mundus MAPP aims to develop graduates who can: Critically analyse policy issues and develop holistic perspectives on European and global governance. Evaluate public policies and policy instruments using quantitative and qualitative methods. Conduct research, analyse data and produce scientifically sound reports. Provide expert advice to decision-makers in national and international settings. Design and participate in the delivery of public policies across different sectors and institutional settings. The programme therefore combines academic study, policy analysis, research, practical experience and international mobility . Mundus MAPP 2027–2029: Application Checklist Before submitting your application, make sure you have: ☐ Selected one mobility track ☐ Checked that you meet the academic requirements ☐ Confirmed that you meet the mobility requirements ☐ Prepared your academic transcripts and degree certificate ☐ Arranged two recommendation letters ☐ Prepared your CV/resume ☐ Written a statement of purpose of 500 words or fewer ☐ Checked the English language requirements ☐ Prepared official English translations where required ☐ Indicated your interest in financial aid if applying by December 1, 2026 ☐ Checked the application deadline for your applicant category ☐ Submitted the complete online application ☐ Followed up with your referees after submission. Official Mundus MAPP Admissions Checklist Apply for the Mundus MAPP 2027–2029 Cohort Applications are currently open for the 2027–2029 Mundus MAPP cohort . Applicants seeking consideration for the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship should submit their application by: December 1, 2026 at 23:59 CET The scholarship provides up to €33,600 over 24 months , calculated at €1,400 per month, together with a full tuition-fee waiver for successful EMJM scholarship recipients. title: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission Mentoring Programme 2026-27: Applications Now Open
summary: Applications are now open for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 , offering Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni the opportunity to connect, share knowledge and skills, build professional networks, and support development impact. The CSC’s Mentoring Programme connects Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to support knowledge and skills development, and provide practical tools to support Scholars in achieving development impact. Why Take Part in the CSC Mentoring Programme? Commonwealth Scholars will have the opportunity to learn from an experienced Commonwealth Alumnus, and gain valuable insights, personalised guidance, and practical advice to help maximise their development impact. Mentees will also be able to build professional connections, receive support in adapting to life and study in the UK, and develop their professional confidence for future career opportunities. Commonwealth Alumni play a key role in shaping a new Scholar’s journey and future impact. As Mentors, they will provide advice on developing new skills and knowledge and applying this learning to drive development impact after the scholarship. The programme offers a rewarding opportunity for Mentors to enhance their mentoring and leadership skills, expand their networks, and share their expertise and experiences within the wider CSC community. The Mentoring Programme runs for one year from December 2026 until December 2027 , with sessions taking place online. How to Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2026. Application Deadline The deadline for applications is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026. You can find out more about the opportunity and read testimonials from previous participants on the CSC Mentoring Programme page . For more information about the eligibility criteria, please read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs . If you have any questions about the CSC Mentoring Programme, or how to apply, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk for more information. CSC Mentoring Programme The Mentoring Programme enables Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to connect and inspire each other to create real-world impact. By matching new Scholars with experienced Alumni working in fields relevant to their studies, the programme offers a unique opportunity for one-on-one guidance and practical insight, helping scholars turn academic knowledge into meaningful action after their Scholarship. How Does the Programme Work? Applications open in August each year, with the programme running from the following January – December (one year cycle). Successful applicants are matched with a Mentor or Mentee whose background and aspirations closely align with their own, ensuring a personalised experience. Your mentoring partnership will progress through five stages, each designed to help you achieve key milestones and make the most of your time together. You’ll be supported throughout the year with programme handbooks, regular communications, and skills development resources, giving you the tools to succeed at every stage. To help you get started and build a productive mentoring partnership, you will be invited to join online information sessions at the beginning of the programme. There’ll also be lively virtual meet-ups where you can connect with other Mentees and Mentors, share your experiences, and build best practice. Who Can Join the CSC Mentoring Programme? Commonwealth Master’s and Doctoral Scholars Become a Mentee and unlock the chance to turn your academic achievements into real-world impact. Through personalised guidance from a Commonwealth Alumnus, you’ll learn how to translate your skills and knowledge into tangible development outcomes back home and gain invaluable insights on navigating life and studies in the UK. As a Mentee, you’ll receive tailored support to help you excel both academically and professionally, with advice on everything from adapting to a new culture to building the employability skills that will set you apart after your Scholarship. Commonwealth Alumni By becoming a Mentor, you’ll play a crucial role in guiding and inspiring the next generation of Scholars, helping them to develop the skills and confidence needed to create meaningful change in their home countries and fields. As a Mentor, you’ll have the rewarding opportunity to share your knowledge and offer practical advice, supporting a Scholar as they navigate their studies and future career. You’ll also expand your own skillset, enhancing your leadership, communication, and mentoring abilities. You will receive information via email when applications open. If you have any questions, you can read our Frequently Asked Questions page or contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk . Why Should I Take Part? To find out what inspired previous Mentors and Mentees to join the programme, read the testimonials below. “The Mentoring Programme exceeded my expectations in most areas, particularly in understanding how to apply my studies for development impact and learning from my Mentor’s expertise as a Commonwealth Scholar. My Mentor provided invaluable insights into practical applications of my field, helping me align my academic goals with real-world challenges. My Mentor also offered excellent professional development advice, which has been instrumental in shaping my career plans. While the advice on living and studying in the UK was helpful, it aligned closely with what I had anticipated. Overall, the programme has been a transformative experience.” 2023 Mentee from India Commonwealth Alumni who have significant professional experience post-Scholarship can volunteer to become a Mentor. As a Mentor, you will have the opportunity to share your expertise to support a new Scholar in developing appropriate skills and knowledge to achieve development impact post-Scholarship and provide advice on how these skills can applied in their home country or home country region. Through the programme, you will develop mentoring and professional skills, such as leadership, communication, and knowledge-sharing. Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing “The CSC Mentoring Programme provided a well-structured platform for personal and professional growth, offering both the resources and guidance necessary to foster meaningful Mentor-Mentee relationships. The programme enabled me to enhance my mentoring skills, while also giving me the opportunity to make a positive impact on my Mentee’s academic, professional, and social development. The collaborative aspect was particularly rewarding, as it allowed me to share knowledge and learn from my Mentee’s fresh perspectives. I feel that the programme successfully met its objectives, and I would recommend it to fellow Alumni seeking to develop as Mentors.” 2023 Mentor from Pakistan How Does the Programme Work? Applications open in September 2025 and pairings will be announced in November 2025. The programme runs for one year from December 2025 to December 2026. Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing Successful applicants are matched in a one-to-one mentoring pairing based on their application responses. The programme consists of 5 stages, which help guide pairs through important milestones to achieve their goals for the programme. Mentees and Mentors will have access to resources including programme handbooks and a range of skills development resources. All participants will have the opportunity to attend virtual information sessions at the start of the programme and virtual meet-up sessions to connect with fellow Mentees and Mentors and share best practice. How Can I Apply? All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2024. You can find out more about the by reading Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) . If you have any questions about the programme, contact the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk . CSC Mentoring Programme Eligibility Who Can Apply to Take Part in the Programme? Mentees All 2026 Commonwealth Scholars studying in the UK Continuing PhD Scholars Mentors All Commonwealth Alumni who have studied in the UK and have at least one year post-Scholarship Current Mentors may apply to take part for another year What Does It Mean If I Apply and Am Not Paired? There are a greater number of eligible Commonwealth Alumni than incoming Scholars. This typically means the programme receives more applications for Mentors than Mentees and as such, not all Mentor applications can be paired. Pairings are made based on application responses across a number of areas, including: pairing country preference; Mentor and Mentee subject and/or field of study; topic area; key words; motivations for becoming a Mentor/Mentee; and the professional experience of a Mentor. Will I Receive Feedback on My Application? We are unable to provide feedback on individual applications. We encourage all unsuccessful applicants to apply to the programme in future, or submit a request to volunteer for any similar opportunities by contacting the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk . About the CSC Mentoring Programme Pairing Will I Have the Same Mentor/Mentee Throughout the Programme? Yes, you will have the same Mentor/Mentee for the duration of the year-long cycle. Will I Be Paired With a Mentor/Mentee From the Same Subject Area? Pairings are based on a range of factors, including home-country or cross-country pairing preference, subject and/or field of study, topic area, key words, motivations for joining the programme, and the Mentor’s professional experience. While subject area and field of study are considered, they are not the primary criteria for pairing. The CSC aims to create pairings that support meaningful knowledge-sharing, professional development, and mentoring relationships. Where possible, applicants will be matched using the information provided in their applications. However, direct matches, where a Mentor and Mentee studied the same subject or attended the same institution, are uncommon and are not the primary aim of the programme. Are All Pairings Successful? During the programme, there is the possibility that not all pairings will continue for the full duration of the programme. In these situations, the Alumni Team will terminate the pairing. Reasons for unsuccessful pairings vary and some are outlined below: Mentor/Mentee has not submitted their agreement form confirming participation Mentor/Mentee is unable to continue due to personal, professional, or other unforeseen commitments Mentor/Mentee mutually agree that the pairing is not suitable The CSC cannot guarantee an alternative pairing if a mentoring pairing ends early. However, participants are encouraged to seek out alternative means of support through CSC activities. What Should a Mentor/Mentee Do If There Is a Disagreement? You should refer to the section on constructive feedback in Mentoring Programme Handbooks available on the CSC website . The information on constructive feedback will support pairs in having healthy and positive mentoring conversations. If you still have any concerns about how to go about this or are unable to reconcile differences, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk . Can a Mentor Engage a Third Person or Expert to Help Their Mentee Regarding a Specific Need? The CSC Mentoring Programme is based on a one-to-one relationship between a Mentor and Mentee. However, where appropriate, a Mentor may recommend or facilitate contact with a third party who can provide specialist advice or expertise relevant to the Mentee’s needs. Before introducing a third party, the Mentor must obtain the consent of both individuals and must not share any personal information, including names or contact details, without their prior agreement. Can Mentors Proof-Read Essays? Mentors can provide guidance, look at sections of work, but should not edit whole chapters or essays, as this is not the purpose of a Mentor. If a Mentee Goes to the Same University as Their Mentor, and Is Doing a Similar Course, Can They Share Notes or Past Exams Papers? This practice can be frowned upon in some UK institutions. Mentees should contact their course coordinator if they wish to view or access these materials. Meeting Your Mentor/Mentee Who Should Initiate the First Introduction? The Mentor should make the first contact by email and introduce themselves to their Mentee. This initial introduction helps establish the mentoring relationship, set expectations, and begin planning future communication. You can read guidance on the type of information to share in initial communications in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks . Is a Physical Meeting Between Mentors and Mentees Allowed? The CSC Mentoring Programme is designed primarily as a virtual programme, as Mentors and Mentees are often based in different countries during the Scholarship period. If a Mentor and Mentee happen to be in the same location and both wish to meet in person, they may do so at their own discretion. Any in-person meeting should be arranged by mutual agreement, take place in a safe and appropriate setting, and comply with any relevant local guidance or regulations (for instance, COVID regulations). Neither Mentor nor Mentee should feel obligated to meet in person, and either party may decline such a meeting if they are uncomfortable doing so. What Is the Minimum Commitment to Meet Every Month? The minimum commitment of engagement is two hours every month. You can organise this time in whatever way works best for your goals and time commitments. Can I Meet With My Mentor/Mentee More Than 2 Hours in a Month? Yes, you can. You will both need to agree meetings and time commitments. What If I Do Not Hear From My Mentor/Mentee? When contacting your Mentor/Mentee, keep in mind that they may have reasons to not respond immediately. The reasons could include important work/study deadlines, travel, illness, or other personal reasons. Always provide a sufficient deadline for them to respond by and if you still fail to hear back, notify the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk . CSC Mentoring Programme Goal Setting What Type of Goals Can I Set? It is important to set clear goals at the start of the cycle so you know what support your Mentor/Mentee needs to provide, and you understand what you can ask them about. Goals may relate to academic, professional, and personal growth. Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks. Should Mentors Set Goals? Yes. The CSC Mentoring Programme is a two-way learning experience, and Mentors are encouraged to set goals for their own development, as well as support their Mentee in achieving theirs. As a Mentor, consider what you hope to gain from the experience, the skills you would like to develop, and what you would like to learn from your Mentee. Examples of Mentor goals include: developing mentorking, leadership and professional skills, building meaningful connections, expanding knowledge of a different sector, country, or professional context, building meaningful connections within the Commonwealth community. Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks. After the CSC Mentoring Programme Will I Get a Certificate for Participating in the Programme? Participants who complete the full mentoring cycle and complete the final feedback survey will receive a certificate confirming their participation. Can Mentors and Mentees Stay in Touch After the Programme? We encourage Mentors and Mentees to discuss whether they would like to keep in contact following the end of the formal programme and you should discuss this during the final stage. It is important to remember that the dynamics of this relationship may be different post-programme. Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 The CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 provides Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni with an opportunity to build meaningful professional connections, exchange knowledge, strengthen mentoring and leadership skills, and support development impact. The application deadline is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026. For further information, visit the CSC Mentoring Programme page and read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs . For questions about the programme or how to apply, contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk .
